Classify like a volunteer

Between 2009 and 2010, 83,943 people answered a tree of questions about 304,122 galaxies for Galaxy Zoo 2. Here are some of those galaxies, as they saw them. Make your call, then see how the volunteers split, and what two neural networks would have said.

Is the galaxy simply smooth and rounded, with no sign of a disk?

Images: SDSS gri composites exactly as shown to Galaxy Zoo 2 volunteers (Willett et al. 2013; Zenodo record 3565489). "Volunteers": consistency-weighted vote fractions; "debiased": corrected for distance by Hart et al. (2016). "Our network": a small CNN trained in this project on 9,000 other GZ2 galaxies; these galaxies were held out of its training. "Zoobot": Walmsley et al. (2023), trained on deeper DESI Legacy Surveys images, which show more disks. Part of the Astrophysics Project Atlas, J2.
